status: Proposal only; no upstream source, guest behavior or trace controls changed
trigger: Actual boot41 had identical stale QMP/VNC console pixels despite real tap and later background/foreground; healthy42 snapshots cannot recover41 submission history.

minimum_events.fields: written value, bit12 schedule decision; cached control/status/enable
minimum_events.question: Did the guest submit a draw?
Did queued work actually execute? Submit writes may legitimately coalesce into one pending BH.

minimum_events.fields: pipe index, explicit disabled/compressed/DMA-failure/drawn outcome, source address/geometry/stride and read length; no pixels
minimum_events.question: Did the callback draw or silently skip an inactive pipe?

minimum_events.fields: status before/after OUTPUT_READY, enable and resulting IRQ level
minimum_events.question: Did display refresh supply readiness while output was stuck?

minimum_events.fields: register kind, written value, old/new status or enable, resulting IRQ level
minimum_events.question: Did the guest acknowledge pending bits or change the interrupt mask?

implementation_constraints: Normal QEMU trace-events disabled by default, fixed allowlist only, bounded existing sole-runner trace window and automatic disable. No unconditional per-frame logging.
Use already available register/read result values; no extra guest memory reads, framebuffer hashing, blocking I/O, timer or interrupt changes.
Trace history counts are observations, not a new hardware counter/register. Record enable/disable completeness; missing disabled intervals cannot prove absent submissions.
Keep original schedule, DMA, pixman, W1C, IRQ and FRAME_PROCESSED behavior exactly unchanged. No redraw workaround.

Capture one healthy path with bounded tracing first; recurrence may then distinguish absent submit, absent BH execution, skipped/failed draw or interrupt acknowledgment history. Healthy-only result is not a reproduced failure.
Existing query-display-registers remains useful at boundaries. Status snapshots alone do not measure frame completion or presentation.
